claim: The two routes to the unified image converge on the same wall, and the wall is the Classic 59,049-cell tape. The arithmetic-image route fails CLOSEST to the limit; the loader route fails further away, and grafting the tuned arithmetic body onto the loader would make it worse, not better.

route_arithmetic_image.attempts: two, 94 then 80 cells short after compression

route_loader_andamio.note: the failure cell is FURTHER from the limit than the arithmetic route's, so this route is further from fitting, not closer

graft_prediction.conclusion: the tuned body of mbir_m2_alu.hell is 100 lines LARGER than the compact from-scratch body already on the loader route, so grafting it would add cells and worsen the 1,430 shortfall

corrected_reading: A failure at cell N means the initializer ran out of room N cells into the address space; the closer N is to 59,049, the closer the image was to fitting.
The arithmetic-image route reached cell 58,969 (80 from the limit); the loader route reached 57,619 (1,430 from the limit). The arithmetic route is therefore the closer one, by a factor of about 18.
My previous message described the loader route as '56 times closer'; that was backwards. The loader route is further from fitting.
why_both_routes_converge: mbir_m2_alu.hell is ALREADY built on the same scaffold: loader-style init, 7-byte load, decrement_value, CARRY, value/value_C1. Its 56,361 bytes are the scaffold plus the tuned arithmetic plus the ADD/SUB dispatch.
The loader's 18,740-byte margin is exactly what the arithmetic engine consumes (56,361 - 40,309 = 16,052), leaving the same 2,688 the arithmetic image has.
Adding one more opcode's dispatch costs more than that margin in either place.
what_would_actually_be_needed: A leaner arithmetic engine: the current one spends 5 result constants (res_is_0/1/2/5/7) selected by flags, plus separate op1/op2 classifications. A comparator that reuses one classification instead of adding a second dispatch would cost less.
Or a smaller domain: the demonstrated operand domain is {0,1,2,3,4}; a comparator restricted to {0,1,2} could share the existing op2 classification instead of adding a 4th/5th opcode decrement.
Or accepting the 59,049-cell limit as the binding constraint and declaring the unified image NOT_DEMONSTRATED, which is what the evidence now supports.
what_is_demonstrated_for_b: The arithmetic half as its own image: mbir_m2_alu.hell loads a 7-byte stored program into RAM and executes ADD/SUB, 8/8 on both engines.
The loader half as its own image: mbir_m2_loader.hell loads prog_0..3 and runs them by PC, 4/4.
Both the load extension to 7 bytes and the opcode dispatch structure assemble on the loader's andamio (unified_loader_gen.py, 9 regions, all structural checks pass).
scope_limits: 'Cells from the limit' is the repo's working interpretation of the initializer failure cell; it is a relative measure, not an exact byte count.
No variant of the arithmetic engine was tuned for size; only the dispatch was varied.
